title: Macronutrient Calculation Methodology
overview: Macronutrient distribution determines how your daily calories are split between protein, carbohydrates, and fats. Different ratios support different goals including weight loss, muscle building, and athletic performance.

methods.name: IIFYM (If It Fits Your Macros)
methods.description: A flexible dieting approach that focuses on meeting macro targets regardless of food source. Popular for sustainability and adherence.

formula.name: Standard IIFYM Distribution
formula.expression:
Protein: 25-30% of calories (1g = 4 cal)
Carbs: 45-55% of calories (1g = 4 cal)
Fat: 20-30% of calories (1g = 9 cal)

methods.name: High-Protein Athletic
methods.description: Recommended by ISSN (International Society of Sports Nutrition) for athletes and those engaged in resistance training.

formula.name: Athletic Macro Distribution
formula.expression:
Protein: 1.6-2.2 g/kg body weight
Carbs: 3-7 g/kg (based on activity)
Fat: 0.5-1.5 g/kg (minimum 20% calories)

variables.meaning: Total body weight for calculation base

limitations: May be excessive for sedentary individuals
Higher cost due to protein sources

methods.name: Ketogenic (Keto)
methods.description: Very low carb, high fat approach that shifts the body into ketosis. Carbs typically limited to 20-50g daily.

formula.name: Ketogenic Ratio
formula.expression:
Fat: 70-75% of calories
Protein: 20-25% of calories
Carbs: 5-10% of calories (20-50g max)

methods.bestFor: Weight loss, epilepsy management, metabolic conditions

methods.name: USDA Dietary Guidelines
methods.description: Official US government recommendations based on Dietary Guidelines for Americans.

formula.name: USDA AMDR
formula.expression:
Protein: 10-35% of calories
Carbs: 45-65% of calories
Fat: 20-35% of calories

footnotes: Protein: 4 calories per gram | Carbs: 4 calories per gram | Fat: 9 calories per gram
Fiber and alcohol have different caloric values (2 and 7 cal/g respectively)
Individual needs vary based on activity, goals, and metabolic factors
disclaimer: Macro recommendations are guidelines. Consult a registered dietitian for personalized nutrition advice, especially if you have health conditions.
